STEP 1 - Scene: A small side salad of mixed leafy greens with shredded carrot and dark thin strips (possibly seaweed or dried mushroom), plus steamed/roasted cauliflower florets on the side.

STEP 2 - Vessel: A white rectangular/square plate, roughly 26 cm across. Area ≈ 3.14 x (13)^2 ≈ 530 cm^2 (a rounded-square plate is similar in area, so I use this value). The glass/table surface and the fork at the left are not food.

STEP 3 - Items:
- Mixed leafy greens (lettuce/kale-type leaves) with shredded carrot and dark strips
- Cauliflower florets (three to four pieces)
- Scattered carrot shreds and small seeds/bits on the plate

STEP 4 - Area:
- Mixed leaves with carrot: ~22% of vessel area (about 115 cm^2)
- Cauliflower: ~12% (about 65 cm^2)
- Scattered carrot bits: ~1% (about 5 cm^2)
Total food coverage ≈ 35% of the plate.

STEP 5 - Volume (gross envelope):
- Leaves: 115 cm^2 x 3 cm ≈ 345 ml
- Cauliflower: 65 cm^2 x 2.5 cm ≈ 163 ml
- Scattered bits: 5 cm^2 x 0.3 cm ≈ 2 ml

STEP 6 - Grams:
- Leaves: 345 ml x 0.15 ≈ 52 g
- Cauliflower (cooked, dense-ish florets): 163 ml x 0.5 ≈ 80 g
- Carrot bits: 2 ml x 0.6 ≈ 1 g

STEP 7 - Energy:
- Leafy greens with carrot: 52 g x 25 kcal/100 g ≈ 13 kcal
- Cauliflower, cooked: 80 g x 25 kcal/100 g ≈ 20 kcal
- Carrot bits: negligible (~0.5 kcal)

STEP 8 - Sanity check: A modest side salad plus a few cauliflower florets on a dinner plate should weigh on the order of 100–150 g and well under 100 kcal. Total ≈ 133 g, ≈ 34 kcal. The dressing is not clearly visible, so no oil is added, which keeps the estimate low; a light dressing could add 20–50 kcal.
